entries.text: Emit FACTORY_BUILD_JSON as the final act of the build stage even when the build is partial or failed, so downstream stages always receive steps/notes instead of a null record.
Have the verify stage hard-fail fast with a captured reason when the build record is absent, rather than propagating an all-null cycle to retro.
Park any pre-existing StarterPack tool into ServerStorage before installing a new weapon so the playtest equips the item under test and the prior rung stays restorable.

After a grip/animation preview lab, explicitly tear down the edit-time weld and re-set Tool.Grip to the final numbers before moving the Tool to StarterPack - a leftover preview weld or lab grip silently ships otherwise.

Roof WedgeParts and angled slabs have easy-to-invert rotation signs (producing a V-valley instead of a pitch) - capture the silhouette from front/iso immediately after placing roof geometry and before any detailing, since the error is invisible in numbers but obvious in one image.

Form real door/window openings by segmenting walls into separate parts around the gap (not by overlaying frames on solid walls) - it makes the building walk-through capable and lets frames/muntins read as depth on capture.

Judge animation filmstrips ONLY by what is visible in the frames: state which way the blade/item points relative to the fist and name one unpredicted detail; a strip where the item is not clearly visible is UNREADABLE and must be re-shot, never passed.
A backlit rig renders as an unjudgeable black silhouette: capture rigs/items with neutralLight=true (capture_animation does this automatically) and re-shoot rather than judge dark frames.

When Cube fails on a niche historical weapon name, re-prompt by describing an analogous familiar object plus explicit shape adjectives (e.g. 'kukri machete, drooping forward-curved blade, hooked bird-head pommel' instead of 'falcata') rather than retrying the same term.
Build wall openings by segmenting the wall into separate parts around each door/window (never overlay a hole part), then verify with a raycast through the opening in edit mode.

Facade trim (timbers, window frames, muntins) must protrude slightly proud of the wall face (~0.15 studs) or it visually vanishes into the wall - check with a first capture_angles pass before detailing further.

Author idle loops as ABSOLUTE full-body keyposes (unlisted joints identity) with the first keyframe re-snapshotted as the last, then verify loop closure numerically (joint-delta between first/last == 0) instead of eyeballing the filmstrip.
Before capture_animation review, temporarily relocate the rig to clear ground with readable colors (then restore position/colors/pose) so filmstrip frames aren't obscured by scene props.

Ground generated/cloned models by computing the bounding-box bottom and offsetting to terrain height, and rescale Cube outputs by setting MeshPart.Size directly since Model:ScaleTo can silently no-op on them.

When dressing a large set-piece, place all props relative to one arena center/radius (torches at fractional radius, perimeter ring with a deliberate gate gap) so composition stays coherent and verifiable from orbit captures.

Load use_rubric(gui)+use_build_guide(gui) BEFORE laying out any ScreenGui and scaffold the rubric's structural baseline first (fullscreen governing root, scale-based sizing with AnchorPoints, a central role-based palette module, a padding system, constraints/TextScaled) - styling an ad-hoc offset layout and evaluating afterward guarantees baseline fails that require a rebuild.

A clean capture/playtest render is visual-presence evidence only, not quality evidence - run evaluate(category) as the pass gate before recording a rung as verified, and bake interaction feedback (hover/press states, tweened panel transitions) into every button/panel at creation time rather than as a polish pass.

Cube-generated weapon meshes can ship an order of magnitude oversized (31 studs here) - rescale MeshPart.Size to hand scale (~2.5-4 studs) immediately after generate_mesh, BEFORE any grip fitting or visual judging, since grip offsets and filmstrip reads are invalid at the wrong scale.

Choose the bind_behavior windup/active timings FIRST and author the use clip's keypose times to land the strike inside that window (e.g. strike keyframe at ~windup+active midpoint), so animation and hit window match without a rework pass.
Build wall openings as real geometry (pier+lintel+sill segments) instead of decals so doors/windows read as true voids from every angle and pass scale checks against the 5-stud character.
After assembling angled roof geometry, capture from a LOW angle specifically to catch parts left floating at the wall-top junction (eave/gable posts) before calling the build done.

Author idle loops as a palindromic keypose sequence (A-B-A-C-D-C-A) so the first and last keyframes are byte-identical, then verify seamlessness numerically by diffing first-vs-last pose transforms instead of eyeballing the filmstrip.

Prevent foot-slide in weight-shift idles by counter-rotating the ankles against the hip/waist roll and never keying foot translation, then verify by asserting foot/lower-leg pose transforms are constant across every keyframe.

Run an interim evaluate/wide-framing capture checkpoint right after the lighting/atmosphere pass and again before dressing is declared done - close-up captures alone can pass while the grader's full-world framing (which includes the plane edge, skirt, and post effects) fails all baselines.

Match set-extension scale to composition: keep the dressed set a dominant fraction of the visible ground plane and give the world edge irregular sculpted falloff, verifying from the widest capture distance rather than only arena-radius shots.
